propositions: rebar comment accepts flag-looking tokens (e.g. --body-file, --body) as positional body argument and stores the literal flag string, silently discarding intended content while exiting 0
commands with positional-only body argument silently truncate surplus positionals via args[:min_args] slice, compounding data loss when a flag token consumes the body slot
the absence of error signal (exit 0, no stderr, comment count incremented) makes silent truncation undetectable until downstream consumers read the corrupted comment body
multiple independent sessions have lost work because the documented write-to-store contract was defeated by the dual-layer loss mechanism
positional-body commands lack a guard against argument tokens beginning with dash, and lack an escape hatch (--) to disambiguate legitimate dash-prefixed values
